materials.material_name: AISI 304 cold-drawn stainless-steel wire reference (true drawing strain 0.585)
materials.manufacturing_condition: Room-temperature multi-pass cold-drawn wire with no intermediate annealing; final diameter 3.55 mm; true drawing strain 0.585; 52.6% area reduction
materials.curve_type: Engineering stress–engineering strain; initial elastic reference plus post-yield points digitized from the monotonic loading curve through the published ultimate tensile point

source_references.title: The effect of drawing strain on the fatigue behaviour of stainless and carbon steel wires (UCT thesis, Fig. 4.23 and Table 4.4, printed pp. 113–114)
source_references.role: Defines the AISI 304 wire chemistry, multi-pass drawing condition, yield strength 1137 MPa, ultimate tensile strength 1346 MPa, total elongation to failure 5%, and the engineering tensile curve used here. The post-elastic plotted points are a documented digitization of the ascending curve shown in Fig. 4.23; Table 4.4 anchors the yield, ultimate, and total-failure-elongation values. The initial linear points use the 193000 MPa room-temperature elastic-modulus reference recorded in this profile.

source_references.title: UCT repository full thesis PDF
source_references.role: Primary document for the drawing schedule, final 3.55 mm diameter, 0.585 true drawing strain, no-intermediate-anneal condition, tensile testing, and curve figure.

source_references.title: SAPIM CX-Ray official product sheet (01 10 2025)
source_references.role: Confirms that the CX-Ray product is described by SAPIM as 18/8 stainless steel and publishes its geometry and 1600 N/mm² middle-strength product value. It does not publish a complete stress–strain curve or certify that the UCT wire state is the CX-Ray production batch.

materials.applicability: This is the explicitly selected AISI 304 cold-drawn reference state for the single-spoke axial model. Every geometry preset uses this same defined material state; selecting a model selects its effective load-bearing cross-sectional area, which is paired with this curve in the stress calculation. Model names do not introduce separate brand material curves.
materials.notes: The calculator interpolates this stored engineering curve to obtain total strain, elastic strain, plastic strain, and permanent elongation after unloading. The initial linear segment is the 193000 MPa elastic-modulus reference; the post-yield points are digitized from UCT Fig. 4.23 and anchored to Table 4.4. Table 4.4 reports 5% total elongation to failure; the calculator exposes that value only as a loaded-length fracture-elongation reference and does not use it to invent a fracture force. The curve is valid only from zero stress through 1346 MPa; work or overload stress above that endpoint is rejected by the backend. No 950 MPa dislocation-threshold parameter is used.
